newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies close mostly lower.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mostly lower on profit taking generally sparked by the premium hog futures currently hold over the CME lean hog index, traders said. Easier cash pork belly prices weighed on pork belly futures, traders said.
Hog futures ended off 0.750 cent a lb to up 0.225 with April off 0.225 at 73.400 cents. June closed off 0.575 at 81.350 cents.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.04 at $72.32 per cwt while June futures started the day at 81.725 cents.
April through July 1998 contracts were up with June and July posting new contract highs.
Pork bellies ended off 0.750 to up 3.000 with May off 0.425 at 78.975 and only the newly traded November fresh contract was up.

Hog futures continued to drift lower awaiting fresh developments from the Taiwan pork ban with the premium of most futures to the index providing pressure. Losses were also attributed to slow pork sales and expecations that packers will likely lower bids for cash hogs in the next couple of days if product prices do not firm, traders said.
But futures held Friday's lows, indicating underlying support, sources noted.
E.D.& F. Man sold June early while Rand Financials, R.J. O'Brien, Rosenthal Collins and ING sold late. Locals and Stone Traders bought late, pit sources said.
In hog options, LFG sold October 70 puts early. There was general offering of June 72 to 76 puts, pit sources added.

Pork bellies ranged on both sides of previous levels and ran up for gains around midday before falling late to new day's lows. Futures held in a technical trading range with ideas on cash also turning mixed, traders said.
Although cash bellies again turned easier after reaching the $75 per cwt area, this setback in cash may be limited.
Seasonal demand is expected to pick up soon for bacon and pork production is seen slipping into the summer. Futures also lack a hedge which will limit any setback, traders added.
The new fresh pork belly settlement price was quoted at $72.32, up $0.70 per cwt.
E.D.&F. Man bought late after selling May on the midday setback and July early. Prudential Securities and Lind-Waldock sold July late, pit sources said.
